chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you see a man who has been afflicted by a trial, say: 'Praise is for Allah Who granted me well-being from that which He afflicted you with, and preferred me over you and over many of those He created,' but do not make him hear what you said.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and supplication when visiting someone who is ill or suffering?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) outlines the etiquette of 'shukr al-ni'ma' (gratitude for blessings) by contrasting one's own safety with another's trial. It emphasizes psychological sensitivity, instructing the believer to recite the praise quietly to avoid causing the afflicted person distress or feeling belittled by the comparison. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing gratitude with empathy, ensuring that recognition of divine favor does not become a source of sorrow for the sufferer.
